clue.text: Period furniture schedule

parts.note: a period is a span of time
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: An antiques dealer's list of period furniture, or a plan for moving it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Period furniture' reads as one antique phrase, but the two words split to give the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: A timetable is a planned schedule of times for trains, lessons or events.

clue.text: Aim to be an instructor

definitions.meaning: to point a gun or camera at a target
to coach or teach someone a skill

explanation.surface: A career ambition: to become a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aim' looks like an ambition, but it is the verb to point at something.
explanation.definitionFit: You train a gun on a target, and a trainer instructs others.

clue.text: Doctor eating every last bit, given a recipe for duck

indicators.note: eating means the doctor's letters surround the rest

parts.note: MD is Doctor of Medicine
all of it, every last bit
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A doctor polishes off the lot after being handed a recipe for duck.
explanation.walkthrough: R for 'recipe' (Latin 'take') is the symbol heading old prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: The mallard is the common wild duck, with the glossy green-headed drake.

clue.text: European flower market's ultimate sugar confection? No resistance!

indicators.note: the last letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the final letter of market

indicators.note: a confection is something made up, so the remaining letters are mixed into a new order
the letter for resistance is removed

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A sweet stall at a European flower market, with no-one resisting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river (something that flows). SUGAR without R leaves SUGA, which 'confection' rearranges to AGUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tagus is the longest river of the Iberian Peninsula, flowing through Spain and Portugal to Lisbon.

clue.text: Secure plum in cases

parts.note: to bag something is to secure or obtain it
a gage is a kind of plum, as in greengage

explanation.surface: Instructions to pack a plum safely into cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plum' looks like a prize, but it is the fruit: a gage.
explanation.definitionFit: Baggage means the cases and bags a traveller carries, collectively luggage.

clue.text: Trip when dancing on cruise, having snatched a kiss

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take hold of the kiss letter inside them
dancing letters move about, so on cruise is rearranged

parts.note: X is the kiss written at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone stealing a kiss while dancing on a cruise trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link word; 'dancing' rearranges ON CRUISE.
explanation.definitionFit: An excursion is a short trip or outing, often for pleasure.

clue.text: Tootsie's pay

definitions.meaning: tootsie is a childish word for a person's lower extremity; the 's is 'is', joining the two senses
to pay a bill is to settle it, as in the phrase about settling the bill

explanation.surface: A question of what Tootsie, perhaps the film character, earns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tootsie' looks like a name (the Dustin Hoffman film), but it is the nursery word for a body part. To 'foot the bill' means to pay it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tootsie is baby talk for that body part, and footing a bill is paying it.

clue.text: Load carried by father figure

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
eight is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A heavy load carried by a father figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'father figure' looks like one phrase, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is goods carried as cargo, a load transported by ship, rail or lorry.

clue.text: Implicit quality of public units

parts.note: overt means open and public
ones are units

explanation.surface: A dry phrase about the hidden character of public bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtones are subtle suggestions or implications beyond the obvious meaning.

clue.text: Idle American Liberal supporter needs muzzle!

parts.note: an ally is someone who supports you
to gag someone is to muzzle them

explanation.surface: An idle American liberal's supporter needs silencing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idle American' is the definition: the word is US slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang, to lallygag is to dawdle or loaf about doing nothing useful.

clue.text: Bar after C sharp

indicators.note: the bar's letters come after the C in the answer

parts.note: a lever is a rigid bar used to prise

explanation.surface: A musical instruction: a bar that follows C sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'C sharp' looks like the musical note, but 'sharp' is the definition and C is taken as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sharp is quick-witted, and that is a synonym for smart.

clue.text: Townswoman on the outskirts of Los Angeles making records

parts.note: Anna is a woman's name and also the name of towns in Illinois and Texas

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges, so only the first and last letters of Los Angeles are used

explanation.surface: A woman from the suburbs of LA turns up in the public records.
explanation.walkthrough: The outskirts of Los Angeles are its first and last letters, L and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Annals are historical records kept year by year.

clue.text: Stop runaway boar colliding with number of spectators

indicators.note: a runaway boar is out of control, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the gate is the attendance count at a sports match

explanation.surface: An escaped boar crashes into a crowd, which needs to be halted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runaway' scrambles BOAR into ABRO; GATE is a British term for the number of people attending a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrogate a law or agreement is to repeal or end it formally.

clue.text: Feeling smart? Make an offer

definitions.meaning: to smart is to sting, so something feeling sore or painful to touch
to put in a formal bid, as for a contract

explanation.surface: Someone who feels clever decides to put in a bid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' reads as clever, but here it means stinging, as in a sore spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruise that is sore to the touch is tender; to bid formally for a contract is to tender.

clue.text: Dismal scientist: "Dynamite to incomes!"

indicators.note: dynamite blows things apart, so the letters of to incomes are scattered

explanation.surface: A gloomy academic declares that incomes are about to boom.
explanation.walkthrough: Carlyle called economics 'the dismal science'.
explanation.definitionFit: Economics is nicknamed the dismal science, so its practitioner is a dismal scientist.

clue.text: Flag — Reuters wrong about dates

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the dates
wrong signals the letters of Reuters are put in another order

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for date, so two of them give DD

explanation.surface: The Reuters news agency is flagged for getting dates wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a verb, but it is the noun. The Red Duster is the red ensign flown by British merchant ships.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Duster is the nickname of the Red Ensign, the British merchant navy flag.

clue.text: Real sexist entertainer on the inside

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters of the words sexist entertainer

explanation.surface: A sexist performer is the genuine article underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Something existent actually exists, so it is real rather than imagined.

clue.text: Passage from never-ending TV soap about bar

indicators.note: the soap's name loses its final letter, so it has no end

parts.note: Corrie is the nickname for Coronation Street, the long-running British TV soap opera

indicators.note: about signals turning the word for bar round

parts.note: a rod is a bar

explanation.surface: A clip from an endless TV soap set in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never-ending' cuts the last letter from CORRIE, giving CORRI; 'about' turns ROD into DOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A corridor is a long passage inside a building, with rooms opening off it.

clue.text: Nasty tear on doll (snapped again?)

indicators.note: a nasty tear mangles things, so the letters of tear are rearranged

parts.note: Ken is Barbie's boyfriend doll

explanation.surface: A nasty rip appears on a doll that may have been broken twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snapped' looks like broken, but it means photographed.
explanation.definitionFit: A photograph snapped a second time has been retaken.

clue.text: Descriptive of K-9's pinch of the ear

parts.note: to pinch is to steal, or rob
otic means relating to the ear

explanation.surface: A dog's party trick of nipping an ear.
explanation.walkthrough: K-9 is the robot dog from Doctor Who, so 'K-9's' looks like a dog's.
explanation.definitionFit: K-9 is a mechanical dog in Doctor Who, so the word for machine-like describes it.

clue.text: Exotic insect is most particular

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange, so the letters of insect are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exotic insect is the fussiest of creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice can mean fussy or finely discriminating, so the most particular is the nicest.

clue.text: Press piece's a bit of a plant?

definitions.meaning: a clipping from a newspaper; the 's is 'is', joining the two senses
a shoot taken from a plant to grow a new one

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a newspaper article was planted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a planted story, but it is a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A press clipping is a newspaper cutting; a slip taken to propagate a plant is also a cutting.

clue.text: Small person failed MOT — having to seek a lift

indicators.note: a car that failed its test is wrecked, so the letters of MOT are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
to thumb a lift is to hitchhike

explanation.surface: A driver whose car failed its MOT has to hitchhike.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for cars; 'failed' rearranges it to TOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of the folk tale, so any very small person.

clue.text: Takes an exam to include finished exercises

indicators.note: the exam word holds the word for finished within it

parts.note: a candidate sits an exam
time is up when it is finished

explanation.surface: A student sitting an exam that includes a section on physical exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: Sit-ups are abdominal exercises done lying on your back and raising your torso.

clue.text: One's captivated by star-shaped feature of fluted column

indicators.note: the one is held inside the reshaped letters
shaped means the letters of star are formed into a new order

parts.note: one gives I, the Roman numeral; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone is captivated by a star-shaped ornament on a fluted column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star-shaped' reads as one adjective, but 'shaped' rearranges STAR into STRA, and I goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A stria is one of the grooves or channels, the flutes, on a column.

clue.text: Penny, dead dishy thing

parts.note: the late person is dead

explanation.surface: Penny, a dead attractive person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dishy' looks like attractive, but it means like a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate is a flat dish to eat from, so a dishy thing in a literal sense.

clue.text: Before extra time starts, Mark gets card

indicators.note: Before tells us the mark's letters go ahead of the starts of extra time

parts.note: a tick is a mark of approval

indicators.note: starts means the opening letters of extra and time are used

explanation.surface: A footballer named Mark is booked just before extra time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' puts the mark ahead of ET. 'card' looks like a referee's booking, but it is a ticket, as in a card of admission.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket is a small printed card or slip giving entry or travel.

clue.text: Doctor finally intervenes in chronic ailment, ending in death

indicators.note: the doctor's piece comes between letters of the other part
chronic means bad, so the letters of ailment are rearranged
finally means the last letter of Doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor at last steps in to treat a chronic ailment that will kill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chronic' rearranges AILMENT into TEMINAL, and R, Doctor's last letter, goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal illness is one that cannot be cured and will result in the patient dying.

clue.text: Takes back gun

indicators.note: back means the word for takes is read from right to left

parts.note: to net something is to catch or take it

explanation.surface: Someone retrieves their firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes back' looks like a single phrase meaning retrieve, but 'back' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sten was a British submachine gun of the Second World War.

clue.text: In general, bustling court figure

indicators.note: In signals that the court abbreviation goes inside the rearranged letters
bustling means busily moving about, so the letters of general are stirred up

explanation.surface: A general bustles about the royal court, cutting a fine figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In general' reads as 'usually', but 'In' is the insertion signal, putting the court abbreviation inside the reshuffled REANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle is a geometric figure with four right angles.
